abstract: Heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME) in lung cancer plays a crucial role in disease progression and resistance to therapy. Despite advances in single-cell and bulk omics profiling, these methods often overlook spatial context, which is vital for understanding cell-cell interactions and regional heterogeneity. In recent years, spatial omics technologies-including spatial genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics-have revolutionized the ability to map molecular landscapes while maintaining tissue architecture. These advancements have become essential components of next-generation lung cancer management. By providing unprecedented resolution in characterizing the lung cancer TME, spatial omics could reveal prognostic and predictive biomarkers and identify new therapeutic vulnerabilities. This review will provide the first critical evaluation of spatial multi-omics approaches for lung cancer prognosis. It will also assess various integration strategies for multi-omics data to explore the clinical translational potential of these tools for therapy selection and patient stratification. Therefore, a deeper understanding of spatial omics technologies and their application in lung cancer can significantly improve precision diagnostics and therapeutic decision-making.
